dc1a6a99f7.why: All four broadcasts and eight stores are required at AVX2 vector widths, and the three scalar updates are live.

ee2be119f9.why: Both broadcasts and all eight stores are required at AVX2 vector widths, along with the pointer and counter updates.

30a0371a13.why: Both loaded vectors, the word difference and its absolute value are required final outputs.

1a270dbc1e.why: Both loaded vectors, both word differences and both absolute values must survive, leaving no removable instruction.

0133dd1f31.why: Each of the four loads, four subtractions and four absolute values produces a required final vector.

febb2405b7.why: The broadcast, shuffle, multiply, add and upper-lane extraction all feed required stores, and both scalar updates are live.

b21195d5f3.why: Each row pair needs its own broadcast, shuffle, rounded multiply and addition, followed by the four required stores and scalar updates.

fdeb071390.why: Four independent broadcast/multiply/add results must be stored, and neither scalar update is dead.

c7cfd35c3e.why: AVX2 cannot fold a memory operand into the minuend of vpsubw, so each independent vector needs its load and subtraction.

04ab3e0953.why: The broadcast is already shared across four required multiply/add/store chains, and the scalar updates are live.

ec4044881b.why: Both arbitrary byte shuffles and wrapping word subtractions are required before the rounded multiplies, and every result feeds a store.

fbf8db589d.why: The unpack and subtraction create distinct word pairs because ymm5 is unconstrained, so all four shuffles and multiply/add/store chains remain necessary.

b4f3f99b7b.why: The two broadcast/subtraction results each feed two independent rounded multiplies, and all additions, stores and scalar updates are live.

4eda8014a4.why: One broadcast/subtraction is already shared by four independent multiply/add/store chains, leaving no removable instruction.

9f77a401f5.why: Arbitrary input vectors require both weighted-sum paths, shifts, saturation and averaging, and the extraction supplies the upper-half stores.

3a6abc2f5a.why: Both weighted sums, logical shifts, saturating pack and unsigned average are required for arbitrary inputs, as are the stores and scalar updates.

vmovdqu ymm7,YMMWORD PTR [rdx+r8*2+0x2]
vmovdqu ymm8,YMMWORD PTR [rax-0x42c]
vperm2i128 ymm9,ymm8,YMMWORD PTR [rax-0x40c],0x31
vperm2i128 ymm8,ymm8,YMMWORD PTR [rax-0x40c],0x20
vpunpcklwd ymm6,ymm7,ymm0
vpunpckhwd ymm7,ymm7,ymm0
af0c6f7bff.why: Load adjacent 128-bit chunks A and B together, then use memory-source lane permutations with chunks C and D to form ymm9=[B,D] and ymm8=[A,C]. This replaces four load/insert instructions with three and reads only bytes loaded originally.

3ae7d7cf06.why: For each four-chunk group, one wide load and two memory-source lane permutations produce the original two interleaved vectors in three instructions instead of four. All loaded bytes and address expressions come from the original accesses.

61bfcd1803.why: All four weighted-sum paths contribute to the two required stores, and arbitrary inputs prevent folding the logical shifts, saturation and averages.
